## Module Objectives

At the end of this module, you should be able to:

- Manage and analyze temporal variables using `lubridate`.
- Study the relationship between two variables using graphs and descriptive statistics, particularly using the correlation coefficient.
- Calculate and interpret the correlation between two numerical variables.
- Write an exploratory data analysis (EDA) report highlighting trends and patterns in the data.

<h3 id="challenge-analyze-delays-to-support-decisions">Challenge — Analyze delays to support decisions</h3>
<p>In this challenge, you must submit a <strong>professional report</strong> intended for your supervisor, <strong>Dr Sofia Martínez</strong>, in order to answer the three major strategic questions posed in the adventure. Your role is to provide clear analysis, supported by relevant visualizations and rigorous interpretations.</p>
<h4 id="what-you-should-do">What you should do</h4>
<p>From the merged data provided (<code>flights_merged_2023.rds</code>), you must:</p>
<ol type="1">
<li><strong>Explore temporal variables</strong> (<code>date</code>, <code>day_week</code>, <code>moment_day</code>, etc.) and prepare them if necessary.</li>
<li><strong>Answer Sofia’s three big questions</strong>:
<ul>
<li>What time slots should you avoid to reduce delays?</li>
<li>To what extent is the weather responsible for the delays?</li>
<li>Are older planes more often delayed or canceled?</li>
</ul></li>
<li>For each question:
<ul>
<li>carry out a relevant <strong>exploratory analysis</strong>;</li>
<li>produce <strong>at least one clear visualization</strong>;</li>
<li>write a <strong>concise interpretation</strong> of your results.</li>
</ul></li>
</ol>
<h4 id="what-the-report-should-contain">What the report should contain</h4>
<p>Your <strong><code>rapport.qmd</code></strong> file must include:</p>
<ul>
<li>A short <strong>introduction</strong> which recalls the context (work at JFK, role with Sofia, etc.).</li>
<li>A section for each <strong>question</strong> of the brief.</li>
<li>Your <strong>analyses</strong> (reproducible R code, tables or graphs, comments).</li>
<li>Your <strong>interpretations</strong> to highlight the key findings.</li>
<li>A <strong>short conclusion</strong> which summarizes the answers given to managers.</li>
</ul>
<h4 id="upload-and-rendering">Upload and rendering</h4>
<ul>
<li>Publish the report to your GitHub repository in the course organization.</li>
<li>Make sure that the <code>.html</code> file is properly generated and readable.</li>
<li>Do a final proofread to check <strong>clarity, structure and presentation</strong>.</li>
</ul>
<blockquote>
<p>Tip: Put yourself in the shoes of a professional analyst — this report could be presented to the airport executive committee!</p>
</blockquote>
